name: Dryosaurus
sum: A fast-running, herbivorous Late Jurassic ornithopod with long slender legs and a stiff tail, known from the Morrison Formation and Europe.
wsnote: Size and growth studies are in question since the largest specimen (CM 1949) was assigned to another species in 2018; no range is given in the sources used.
holotype: Not read in the sources consulted; first remains found by S. W. Williston in 1876 in Albany County, Wyoming, and named by O. C. Marsh in 1878.
material: Many specimens, including a second species, Dryosaurus elderae, named by Carpenter and Galton in 2018.
biology: A long neck, long slender legs and a long stiff tail, a horny beak and cheek teeth with a strong median ridge on the outer surface; the genus name refers to a forested habitat.
author: Marsh 1894
